x-post v/magictcg: Magic Origins Standard: G/B midrange- Critiques Wanted

It's hard to make any real comments without any testing and results behind it and knowing the decks good and bad match ups. So these are just my observations from just looking at the deck list.

Before I get too detailed about specific card choices I'll make a few broader comments. The deck is too in between mid range and control. Midrange takes advantage of games by playing big efficient creatures fast. Currently your best play with a nut draw would be a turn three sidisi or Tas. That's good but by no means back breaking. You have no evasion, and you don't do anything particularly better than already existing decks. Megamorphs and devotion play a better midrange game and abzan and ub play a better control. On to card choices.

Languish: I don't like this card in this deck. This card kills every single one of your creature besides Sidisi and Tas. Maybe a sb card, but I still don't know.

Sidisi: This is a great card, but 4 of is too many. The fact that it's legendary makes me want to play less than 4 to start. You also don't have many things I want to be searching for that would require 4. I think 2 is probably good number, 3 if you really like the card.

Ugin: Great card and can definitely take advantage of your mama, but again I don't feel it's where you want to be. You really can't take advantage of his board wipe without attaching your own board. If you are set on playing him I think whisperwood is an automatic include. Also 1 is more than enough.

So I tried to keep true to your theme and make it a little more aggro/midrange. This list is still very rough and just something I put together while I'm at work:
Cretures
4x elvish mystic
3x warden of the first tree
4x death dealer
4x courser of kruphix
3x den protecter
3x nissa
3x polukranos
4x whisperwood elemental

Spells
4x heros downfall
4x thoughtseize
1x Ugin

Lands

4xLlanowar Wastes
4x Temple of Malady
4x Windswept heath
5x Forest
5x Swamp
1x Urborg

I added some small resilient creatures like warden and death dealer, who also work as good mana sinks. Polyk is in there for a turn 3 drop off of a mystic and a sink for mana. I also felt that courser and nissa was enough of land filters to not warrant read that bones. I could be wrong about that though. I added in 4 fetch lands so you could flip nissa at instant speed. This allows for so dodging of removal spells and blocking combat tricks.

Thanks for your analysis I appreciate it.

The main thing this deck does better than abzan is that it has access to elvish mystic, which is a significant appeal as the card is very powerful.

Abzan decks have usually run 2 crux of fate, and they have the same situaitionalness that is present in this deck with languish, but it is still a good inclusion there and here I believe. Its an excellent card when playing the control role.

I've playtested the deck on the mtgo beta (where you have a standard god account incl origins cards) and i haven't run into the languish issue you describe. I have had situations where I find myself with a sidisi to spare, but being able to exploit your wayfinders and mystics is a good thing. I'd be fine with less than 4 but its not egregious so far.

Thats an interesting idea with fetchlands to flip Nissa, I havent thought of that!

I think the odd man out of your decklist is the warden. I get that its a mana sink but i don't think 24 lands plus 4 mystics is a good recipie with warden. An opening hand of mystic and warden and land and a downfall and denprotector for example seems more disjoined/unfocused than a hand of mystic, downfall, read the bones, den protector and land.

You have access to elvish mystic but in your list you don't take much advantage of it. Without being able to put out a powerful 4 drop on turn 3 mystic just seems bad. Abzan used to play mystic but they don't anymore. The reason abzan doesn't play it is because it's a terrible late game top deck and they moved more to control over mid range type strategy.
You must not have played many games because you have 6 creatures in your entire deck that survive languish and they are both legendary. That means at best you will only ever have 2 creatures survive that spell. It's not the direction you want to be going in.
Agree that warden is out of place in this list, but you are making a bunch of mana and not doing anything with it. You have to utilize it somehow otherwise you aren't really doing much of anything but flipping nissa.

I think the reason Abzan doesn't play mystic is because it can't reliably cast it. Being able to cast three drops on turn two and five drop on turn 4 (etc etc) seem like a good use of mystic still. Cards like thoughtseize are poor late game draws but that alone doesn't prevent a deck like abzan from playing the card, the cost/benefit works out on it. Here too I think the cost of drawing mystic late is mitigated both by the large benefit incurred when it is drawn early in other games, as well as the existence of sidisi in the deck making the mystic exchange for a tutor effect at times when drawn late.

So far in my experience ive really liked the languish being in the deck, but you are correct that the sample size is small.

Abzan can cast mystic turn one. Idk where you are getting your facts from but being able to cast courser turn three means they can absolutely cast mystic turn one. They used to main deck mystic so you are basically telling me you are making decks and choices off of opinions and experience and not actually testing and facts. Mystic is a terrible top deck late game. Especially when Abazans game plan is to have better top decks than you. Yes thoughtseize late game isn't great but it has it uses, especially against control. Mystic is a terrible draw late game and you don't take advantage of its early game so it's useless in your deck.
